items.q: What is the difference between a strong acid and a concentrated acid?
items.correct: Strong = fully ionised; concentrated = a lot of acid per volume.
items.random_wrong: Concentration has no effect on how an acid behaves.
items.why: Strength is about degree of ionisation; concentration is about amount dissolved — a weak acid can still be concentrated.
Acids are below pH 7, alkalis above 7, neutral is 7.

items.correct: Moves the pH towards 7, forming a salt and water.
items.random_wrong: Produces only water and nothing else.
items.why: Acid + base → salt + water; the mixture moves towards neutral.
